content: The content provided appears to be a detailed list of studies, guidelines, and research questions related to the prevention of bloodstream infections (BSIs) and complications associated with the use of intravascular catheters, including peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVCs), peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs), and other vascular access devices. 1. A multicenter study evaluated the effectiveness of a multimodal intervention aimed at reducing bloodstream infections associated with vascular catheters in non-ICU wards. The findings were published in Clinical Microbiology and Infection in 2013. 2. Garcia-Gasalla et al. conducted a study on the outcomes of a multi-faceted educational intervention to prevent bloodstream infections related to peripheral venous catheters. The results were published in Journal of Hospital Infection in 2019. 3. Gunasegaran et al. performed a randomized controlled trial to assess the effectiveness of two treatment methods in reducing the incidence of phlebitis associated with short peripheral catheters. The study was published in Journal of Infusion Nursing in 2018. 4. Gupta et al. compared the efficacy of recommended practices for peripheral intravenous cannula insertion with a standard protocol in a randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in Medical Journal Armed Forces India in 2022. 5. Hontoria-Alcoceba et al. implemented evidence-based practices for the care of peripheral intravenous catheters, with results published in Journal of Nursing Care Quality in 2023. 6. Jong Hee O et al. described the implementation of clinical practice guidelines for replacing peripheral intravenous catheters, published in Journal of Nursing Care Quality in 2020. 7. Kleidon et al. reported on the implementation of a pediatric peripheral intravenous catheter care bundle as part of a quality improvement initiative. The study was published in Journal of Paediatrics and Child Health in 2019. 8. Kollar explored strategies to optimize the effectiveness of short peripheral catheters, with findings published in Journal of Infusion Nursing in 2021. 9. Krempser et al. developed a nursing protocol for vascular trauma prevention using a peripheral catheterization bundle in emergency settings. The study was published in Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem in 2019. 10. Lolom et al. investigated the impact of a long-term quality improvement program on reducing infection risks associated with peripheral venous catheters. The findings were published in Presse Médicale in 2009. 11. Lundgren and Wahren examined the effect of education on evidence-based care and handling of peripheral intravenous lines, with results published in Journal of Clinical Nursing in 1999. 12. Murayama et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to verify the effectiveness of a new long peripheral intravenous catheter for upper arm vein catheterization in reducing catheter failure. The study was published in Drug Discoveries & Therapeutics in 2023. 13. Parreira et al. evaluated the impact of an innovative securement dressing and tourniquet on complications and contamination related to peripheral intravenous catheters. The study was published in International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2019. 14. Phan et al. reported on enhanced infection control interventions that reduced catheter-related bloodstream infections in the neonatal department of Hung Vuong Hospital, Vietnam, in a preand post-intervention study published in Antimicrobial Resistance & Infection Control in 2020. 15. Rhodes et al. successfully implemented a care bundle to reduce Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections associated with peripheral intravenous cannulae in a large Australian health service. The findings were published in Journal of Hospital Infection in 2016. 16. Salm et al. described the implementation of an evidence-based bundle for bloodstream infections in neonatal intensive care units in Germany, with results published in Infection Control & Hospital Epidemiology in 2016. 17. Sriupayo et al. assessed the effectiveness of a peripheral vascular catheter care bundle in pediatric nursing services at Chiang Mai University Hospital, Thailand. 18. Steere et al. implemented the PIV5Rights™ bundle, a lean multimodal strategy to achieve one peripheral intravenous catheter per patient visit. The study was published in Journal of the Association for Vascular Access in 2019. 19. Takahashi et al. investigated methods to prevent peripheral intravenous catheter failure by reducing mechanical irritation, with findings published in Scientific Reports in 2020. 20. Vergara et al. shared lessons from an interventional program addressing infectious and non-infectious phlebitis associated with peripheral venous catheters. The study was published in Revista Chilena de Infectología in 2017. 21. Aly et al. explored whether bloodstream infections are preventable among premature infants in a comparative study of two cities, published in Pediatrics in 2005. 22. Arnts et al. demonstrated that central line bloodstream infections in newborns can be reduced using the modified Seldinger technique and care bundles. The study was published in Acta Paediatrica in 2015. 23. Bayoumi et al. evaluated the effect of implementing an epicutaneo-caval catheter team in a neonatal intensive care unit, with findings published in Journal of Vascular Access in 2021. 24. Costa et al. identified risk factors for bloodstream infections associated with peripherally inserted central catheters in neonates, published in Acta Paulista de Enfermagem in 2016. 25. Eturajulu et al. described a quality improvement report on a safety program for preventing central line-associated bloodstream infections, published in Radiographics in 2022. 26. Golombek et al. reported that proactive management of percutaneously inserted central catheters reduced infection incidence in extremely low birth weight populations. The study was published in Journal of Perinatology in 2002. 27. Harnage achieved zero catheter-related bloodstream infections over 15 months in a community-based medical center, with results published in Journal of the Association for Vascular Access in 2007. 28. He et al. evaluated the therapeutic effect of ultrasound-guided peripherally inserted central catheters combined with predictive nursing in patients with severe burns. The study was published in Computational and Mathematical Methods in Medicine in 2022. 29. Jia investigated the influence of clustered nursing interventions on complications of peripherally inserted central catheters, published in Chinese Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2017. 30. Kaplan et al. described a statewide quality improvement collaborative in Ohio to reduce late-onset sepsis in preterm infants, published in Pediatrics in 2011. 31. Ma et al. applied a risk prevention management system in cervical cancer patients undergoing PICC catheterization for chemotherapy, with findings published in Chinese Nursing Research in 2020. 32. Liu et al. explored evidence-based nursing practices to prevent postoperative complications with PICC insertion, published in Chinese Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2013. 33. Dorea et al. examined complications related to the type of epicutaneous catheter in neonates, published in Online Brazilian Journal of Nursing in 2013. 34. Royer implemented a better bundle to achieve and sustain zero central line-associated bloodstream infection rates, published in Journal of Infusion Nursing in 2010. 35. Schelonka et al. reported sustained reductions in neonatal nosocomial infection rates following a comprehensive infection control intervention, published in Journal of Perinatology in 2006. 36. Sherrod et al. designed and monitored an RN-based PICC team, with findings published in Neonatal Intensive Care in 2004. 37. Steiner et al. demonstrated a significant reduction in catheter-associated bloodstream infections in preterm neonates after implementing a care bundle focusing on simulation training for central line insertion. The study was published in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2015. 38. Swaminathan et al. improved PICC use and outcomes in hospitalized patients through an interrupted time series study using MAGIC criteria, published in BMJ Quality & Safety in 2018. 39. Taylor et al. evaluated the effect of a dedicated PICC team on neonatal catheter-related bloodstream infections, published in Advances in Neonatal Care in 2011. 40. Thibodeau et al. assessed the effectiveness of a new flushing and maintenance policy for PICCs in adults, published in Journal of Infusion Nursing in 2007. 41. Tian et al. evaluated the efficacy of multifaceted interventions in reducing complications of PICCs in adult oncology patients, published in Supportive Care in Cancer in 2010. 42. Tong et al. investigated process management strategies to prevent bloodstream infections related to peripheral central venous catheters, published in Chinese Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2011. 43. Wang et al. demonstrated the prevention of PICC-associated bloodstream infections in very low birth weight infants using a central line bundle guideline with a standard checklist, published in BMC Pediatrics in 2015. 44. Silva et al. compared PICCs placed and maintained by a dedicated nursing team for antimicrobial therapy versus other catheter types in a retrospective case-control study, published in Enfermedades Infecciosas y Microbiología Clínica in 2020. 45. Yuan et al. evaluated the prevention of PICC-related infections in very low birth weight infants using a central line bundle guideline with a standard checklist, published in International Journal of Nursing Sciences in 2016. 46. Hoyer et al. explored the use of ultrasound-guided procedures in medical education, published in International Emergency Medicine in 2016. 47. Grayson et al. assessed the effects of the Australian National Hand Hygiene Initiative on infection control practices, healthcare worker education, and clinical outcomes over eight years, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2018. 48. Allegretti et al. evaluated the global implementation of WHO's multimodal strategy for improving hand hygiene in a quasi-experimental study, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2013. This summary provides a detailed overview of the studies and interventions aimed at improving catheter care and reducing infection risks.
